name: Greek Tomato Fritters

cookwares.name: blender or food processor or box grater
10 inch cast iron skillet or Dutch oven,1/4 cup measuring cup

ingredients.name: fresh flat leaf parsley leaves, tender stems roughly chopped

instructions.primary_message: For the Batter: Coarsely chop 227 g tomatoes (about 2 tomatoes) and either gently pulse in blender or food processor until just combined or shred on large holes of box grater set over a bowl, flesh side facing the blades.

Carefully chop any excess tomato skin after shredding. Transfer shredded tomato to a large bowl. Dice remaining 113 g tomato (about 1 tomato) into 0.5 cm pieces, and add to bowl with shredded tomato. (You should have about 1 1/2 cups tomatoes.)

Add onion, feta, parsley, dill, thyme, dried oregano or marjoram, egg, salt, and pepper to tomatoes and stir to combine. Use the back of a large spoon to break feta into blueberry-sized chunks. Slowly start adding flour 1/4 cup at a time, until fritter batter is loose but not runny, similar in consistency to a loose tuna salad. Batter should be set enough to scoop and rest on a spoon and barely hold its form without falling off, but not overly thick or cakey. Set aside.

For Frying the Fritters: Line a rimmed baking sheet with a double layer of paper towels and set aside. In a 25-cm cast iron skillet or Dutch oven, add oil (oil should measure 2.5 to 4 cm deep) and heat on medium-high until oil registers 175°C on an instant-read or deep-fry thermometer. Once oil reaches 177°C, lower heat to medium. Using a 1/4-cup dry measuring cup, drop five 1/4-cup portions of batter into pan, evenly spaced apart, using a spoon to gently transfer batter into hot oil.

Fry, adjusting heat as needed to maintain oil temperature around 300 to 177°C (150 to 175°C). Note that some loud, vigorous bubbling is common when fritters make initial contact with oil. Fry fritters for 10 seconds, then give a gentle nudge underneath with a fork to ensure they are not sticking to bottom of pan. They should slightly puff up and float when frying. Fry until deep golden brown on the exterior and yellow-orange on the inside, 3 to 5 minutes per side.

Use a slotted spoon to transfer fritters, letting excess oil drain into skillet, to prepared baking sheet. Sprinkle lightly with salt and let sit for at least 2 minutes to cool. Return oil to 175°C (350°F), adjusting heat as needed, and repeat frying fritters in batches of 5 at a time. Let the last batch sit for 2 minutes after removing from oil, then serve immediately, accompanied by a side of yogurt for dipping, if desired.

schema_metadata.keywords: tomato fritters recipe, vegetable fritters, fritter, greek tomato fritters

description: These juicy, golden tomato fritters from the Greek islands are packed with herbs, briny feta, and peak-summer flavor.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Plain whole-milk strained (Greek-style) yogurt for serving, optional

Optional substitutions: dried oregano → marjoram

Notes: Choose an oil with a high smoke point. I recommend safflower, sunflower or avocado oil, as they are neutral in flavor.
Sheep’s milk feta or sheep’s milk feta with some goat milk, packaged in brine, best resembles the flavor of Greek feta. Cow’s milk feta is typically dry and does not offer a comparably creamy, briny flavor.

Make-ahead and storage: The tomatoes, fresh herbs, and onion can be chopped up to 1 day ahead and stored in separate airtight containers in the refrigerator.
The fritters are best served immediately, but leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat on a parchment paper-lined rimmed baking sheet in a 180°C (350°F) oven until recrisped and heated through, 5 to 7 minutes.
author: Sharon Brenner
